A1.justification: Despite the title changing from Code2Logic to Game-RL, both PDFs describe the same Code2Logic pipeline, GameQA dataset, and training experiments. Their text, tables, equations, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original GRPO and SFT experiments, benchmark evaluations, scaling studies, human-baseline results, and error analyses, including in its appendices.

after.justification: V4 retains these original empirical results and adds evaluated training-data comparators and Claude-4-Sonnet results.

M1.justification: The code-construction, template-design, and data-engine pipeline remains unchanged, as does GRPO with an LLM-judged binary outcome reward. Game-RL names the existing training approach. Splitting action-sequence generation and execution into separate explanatory modules does not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: V4 newly uses MAVIS geometry/function data for comparison training. GameQA's 30 games and 158 tasks and the seven external evaluation benchmarks remain unchanged. MultiMath was already represented in v2's Geo-Multi SFT data; its standalone RL comparison does not introduce an entirely new domain.

E2.justification: Table 5 adds GRPO training on MAVIS and standalone MultiMath-8K alongside the retained Multimodal-Open-R1 comparison. Tables 3 and 6 add Claude-4-Sonnet and remove Qwen2-VL-72B. The remaining comparator membership is retained.

E3.justification: The new MAVIS control introduces sampling from geometry/function splits, with 8k training samples reported in Section 5.5. Appendix C.2.2's description of sampling 4k does not clearly specify whether this means per split. Retained experiments preserve their evaluation procedures; newly stated rollout and epoch counts are disclosures, not established setting changes.

E4.justification: Appendix B.1 updates the evidence on sensitivity to question difficulty and image complexity by adding Claude-4-Sonnet and removing Qwen2-VL-72B in Table 6. The game-diversity and sample-reuse studies, SFT comparisons, error analyses, and detailed case studies are otherwise retained.

E5.justification: Both versions select the best validation checkpoint for main/SFT experiments and average three validation-selected checkpoints from ten saved checkpoints for other experiments. Neither adds independent repeated-run reporting, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The newly disclosed rollout count is not an uncertainty-reporting change.

E6.justification: Retained numerical rows in Tables 3–6 and 8–9 are unchanged. New Table 5 entries report general-benchmark averages of 51.53 for MAVIS and 52.81 for MultiMath-8K, alongside GameQA's unchanged 52.31; GameQA retains the highest out-of-domain game average there. Claude-4-Sonnet results are added and Qwen2-VL-72B results removed.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 newly provides an explicit mathematical definition of the standard clipped GRPO objective with KL regularization; v2 only identifies the algorithm. The binary-reward equation restates v2 Appendix C.4. This is a limited formal addition without new proofs or theoretical guarantees.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction replace scarce CoT data with narrow RL task diversity as the principal problem and foreground verifiable game tasks and Game-RL. The central Code2Logic/GameQA contributions and the claimed 2.33 improvement across seven benchmarks remain.

C2.justification: V4 extends the transfer discussion to MAVIS geometry/function training and drops v2 Appendix C.4's assertion that quantizing the reward judge improves speed while preserving accuracy and consistency. The overfitting explanations, game failure mechanisms, and Appendix A limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V4 newly specifies 12 rollouts per question, clipping at 0.2, and one-epoch main SFT/GRPO training. Condensed Appendices E.4 and F.3 omit details such as Spider Solitaire initialization ranges and reference-step consistency checks. Hardware, training times, prompts, and repository access are retained; MultiMath-8K preparation remains unexplained.

R1.justification: V4 adds the LLaVA-OneVision reference and removes Bring Reason to Vision and the Qwen2.5-Math report. Positioning shifts toward diverse, verifiable RL tasks, including a verifiability comparison in Table 1. Most related-work discussion remains unchanged; VideoGameBench's updated citation represents the same work.

P1.justification: V4 substantially rewrites the abstract, introduction, and method narrative, adopts task-template terminology, and introduces a dedicated Game-RL section. Experimental settings move into the main text, qualitative summaries are consolidated in Appendix I, and implementation and quality-assurance appendices are substantially condensed.

P2.justification: V4 adopts a substantially different visual template, including institutional logos, a shaded abstract, blue headings, and revised typography and spacing. The dataset overview moves from Figure 5 near the appendices to main-text Figure 3; figures are resized and reordered, Table 1 gains a verifiability column, and comparison tables gain rows.

improvement.justification: The added training-data controls provide a better basis for assessing generalization, while rollout, clipping, and epoch disclosures improve reproducibility. These are limited gains: Section 5.5 does not discuss MultiMath's higher Table 5 general average, MAVIS sampling is ambiguously documented, and some generation and quality-control details are lost. The core method and main results remain stable.
